headline: Zia assassination: Muzaffar to face court martial
summary: Major (retd) Md Muzaffar Hossain, arrested in connection with the 1981 killing of former president Ziaur Rahman, will be tried under military law.
details: Major (retd) Md Muzaffar Hossain has been handed over to the Bangladesh Army to face trial through a general court martial under military law, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed announced today.
Muzaffar had been absconding for decades under a different identity in a neighbouring country after a court of inquiry recommended military proceedings against him.
Law enforcement agencies arrested him following intelligence reports that he had returned to Bangladesh.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that the military process should conclude first before the government considers filing fresh criminal cases or investigating other alleged accomplices.
The minister also clarified that military personnel are subject to the Armed Forces Act and cannot be tried twice for the same offence under different laws.
caption:
Absconding for decades under a fake identity, a retired Major is now facing a court martial for the 1981 assassination of President Ziaur Rahman.

Major (retd) Md Muzaffar Hossain has been handed over to the Bangladesh Army to face trial through a general court martial under military law, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed announced today.

Muzaffar had been absconding for decades under a different identity in a neighbouring country after a court of inquiry recommended military proceedings against him.

Law enforcement agencies arrested him following intelligence reports that he had returned to Bangladesh.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that the military process should conclude first before the government considers filing fresh criminal cases or investigating other alleged accomplices.

The minister also clarified that military personnel are subject to the Armed Forces Act and cannot be tried twice for the same offence under different laws.

headline_marked: 40 villages [[flooded in Netrakona]] as hill water flows from India
headline: 40 villages flooded in Netrakona as hill water flows from India
summary: Flash floods triggered by heavy rainfall in Meghalaya have submerged roads and houses, with one river flowing above the danger level.
details: Heavy rainfall and hill water flowing from India's Meghalaya state triggered flash floods in the border upazilas of Kalmakanda and Durgapur in Netrakona yesterday.
At least 40 villages have been inundated, with water entering houses and submerging main roads, disrupting communication in several areas.
According to the Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB), water levels in almost all rivers in Netrakona are rising rapidly.
The Updakhali river in Kalmakanda is currently flowing 15 centimetres above the danger level and may rise further.
Local residents report that water entered with tremendous force through the Mongleshwari river and canals, washing away fish from numerous ponds.
The upazila administration has sent teams to inspect the affected areas to assess the full extent of the damage.
Local authorities state they are prepared to respond to the ongoing flash flood situation.
caption:
40 villages submerged as hill water from India surges into Netrakona.

Heavy rainfall and hill water flowing from India's Meghalaya state triggered flash floods in the border upazilas of Kalmakanda and Durgapur in Netrakona yesterday.

At least 40 villages have been inundated, with water entering houses and submerging main roads, disrupting communication in several areas.

According to the Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB), water levels in almost all rivers in Netrakona are rising rapidly.

The Updakhali river in Kalmakanda is currently flowing 15 centimetres above the danger level and may rise further.

Local residents report that water entered with tremendous force through the Mongleshwari river and canals, washing away fish from numerous ponds.

The upazila administration has sent teams to inspect the affected areas to assess the full extent of the damage.

Local authorities state they are prepared to respond to the ongoing flash flood situation.
